name: Physiotherapy for Back Pain
summary: Research suggests 80% of adults experience lower back pain, most often from sedentary lifestyles. Pain may originate from muscle, ligament or nerve — our team identifies the true source and treats it with manual therapy, dry needling and physio modalities.
symptoms_html:
• Dull ache or sharp pain in the lower, mid or upper back
  • Pain radiating from buttock to foot (sciatica) with numbness or burning
  • Stiffness after sitting or standing for long periods
  • Muscle spasm and reduced flexibility
  • Pain that worsens with bending, lifting or poor posture
causes_html:
• Sedentary lifestyle — prolonged hunched sitting weakens spinal support muscles
  • Disc bulge or herniation — compressing the sciatic nerve
  • Poor posture — wrong lifting technique, bad mattress, slouched workstation
  • Pregnancy & postpartum — hormonal loosening and added load on back muscles
  • Arthritis — osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis affecting spinal joints
treatment_html:
Back pain is the most common problem we treat. Pain can originate from muscle, ligament or nerve depending on the underlying cause — which is why accurate assessment comes first. The KR physiotherapy team follows all the manual therapies including mobilisation, chiropractic, dry needling and cupping, and provides treatment by physio modalities as needed.

Back pain with sciatica

Sciatic nerve compression from a disc bulge or herniation can cause pain from the buttock to the foot along with numbness, weakness or burning. Physiotherapy is the best line of treatment — we use chiropractic, cupping therapy and manual therapy to relieve it.

Back pain due to bad posture

Prolonged sitting, lifting in the wrong posture and lying on a bad mattress stress back muscles and ligaments. We guide you on correct posture at your workspace and in daily activity to cure and prevent recurrence.

Back pain due to pregnancy

Hormones during pregnancy weaken muscles and ligaments while the growing bump loads the back. Our female physiotherapist provides specialised postpartum back-pain treatment.

Back pain due to arthritis

Inflammation of spinal joints — osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis — responds well to ultrasound, TENS, IFT and manual therapy, all available in-clinic. We use single or combined treatment lines based on your rehabilitation programme.

name: Physiotherapy for Shoulder Pain
summary: Injury, arthritis, frozen shoulder, strain/sprain or dislocation can all cause shoulder pain. We identify the underlying cause — impingement, frozen shoulder or rotator cuff injury — and treat it with manual therapy and targeted rehabilitation.
symptoms_html:
• Pain on lifting the arm overhead or behind the back
  • Stiffness and reduced range of motion (frozen shoulder)
  • Weakness when lifting or rotating the arm
  • Pain at night, especially lying on the affected side
  • Clicking, catching or instability in the joint
causes_html:
• Impingement — repetitive overhead movement pinching shoulder tendons
  • Frozen shoulder — progressive stiffening and pain, common after injury or immobilisation
  • Rotator cuff injury — strain or tear of the stabilising tendons
  • Arthritis — wear of the joint cartilage
  • Strain/sprain or dislocation — sports falls and accidents
treatment_html:
Do you have shoulder pain? KR Physiotherapy gives you the best advice and treatment. We assess the underlying cause and treat it directly — any kind of injury, arthritis, frozen shoulder, strain/sprain or dislocation of the shoulder can be helped.

Shoulder impingement

Repetitive shoulder movement can cause impingement, which responds very well to physiotherapy. We rebuild muscle strength and range of motion so you recover faster.

Frozen shoulder

One of the most common causes of shoulder pain. We care for many patients with frozen shoulder, using progressive mobilisation and stretching to restore movement.

Rotator cuff injury

If you are suffering from a rotator cuff injury or tear, physiotherapy is the best route to healing. Our clinic follows all the manual therapies for treating shoulder pain — helping you avoid surgery wherever possible.

name: Physiotherapy for Knee Pain
summary: The knee is the largest and most complex joint in the body. Injury, arthritis, overuse, aging, mechanical problems and medical conditions all cause knee pain — physiotherapy addresses the root cause non-surgically.
symptoms_html:
• Pain behind or around the kneecap, sometimes travelling to thigh or shin
  • Swelling and inflammation around the joint
  • Stiffness — difficulty bending or straightening the knee
  • Redness and warmth over the joint
  • Clicking or popping sounds during movement
  • Giving way or inability to bear weight
causes_html:
• Injuries — ACL injury, fractures, torn meniscus, bursitis, sprains, patellar tendinitis
  • Arthritis — osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, pseudogout, septic arthritis
  • Overuse — repetitive stress common in runners and cyclists
  • Aging — gradual wear of joint structures and bony growths
  • Mechanical problems — loose bodies, IT band syndrome, dislocated kneecap, foot or hip pain referring to the knee
treatment_html:
The appropriate plan depends on the cause and severity of your knee pain. Common approaches include rest, ice therapy, supportive bracing and — most importantly — structured physiotherapy.

How physiotherapy reduces knee pain

Physiotherapy is a proven, non-invasive approach that addresses the underlying causes and promotes joint health:

  • Pain management — ice/heat therapy and TENS to control pain and inflammation
  • Manual therapy — hands-on techniques and soft-tissue massage to restore range of motion
  • Strengthening exercises — targeted muscle work around the knee for joint stability
  • Patient education — posture and body mechanics to reduce daily joint stress
  • Custom plans and home programmes — tailored to your specific condition with exercises to continue at home

We provide the best physiotherapy treatment for knee pain in Noida and nearby areas — call us to book an appointment for any knee-related problem.

name: Physiotherapy for Neck Pain
summary: Physiotherapy is the most effective treatment for neck pain — eliminating pain and discomfort so you can live freely. We assess the cause: poor posture, sedentary lifestyle, injury or age-related changes.
symptoms_html:
• Heaviness and pain in the cervical spine and arm
  • Headache, dizziness or vertigo
  • Pain radiating down the arm, with or without tingling
  • Soreness and mild swelling around the neck
  • Reduced ability to turn or tilt the head
causes_html:
• Degeneration — age-related wear of the cervical spine
  • Injury — trauma such as whiplash
  • Poor posture — long sitting hours, overuse of mobile and computer
  • Excess weight — overstressed back and neck muscles
treatment_html:
Neck pain is felt behind the head in the cervical spine and surrounding area, and can combine with headache, dizziness and arm symptoms. Left untreated it can lead to secondary problems — persistent headaches, radiating arm pain and reduced head movement — so early physiotherapy matters.

How physiotherapy helps

Our physiotherapists strengthen your neck and shoulder muscles so overstress-related pain reduces. Mobilisation, chiropractic, dry needling and electrotherapy (US, SWD, TENS) all play important roles. We first assess you to rule out the possible cause, then plan treatment accordingly — most patients see lasting relief without any medication.

When is neck pain serious?

If pain does not settle within a few days, or radiates into your arm with numbness, consult a physiotherapist promptly. Our team will assess and treat the root cause before it becomes chronic.

name: Knee Ligament Injuries
summary: Knee ligaments connect thigh bone to lower leg bone. Tears and sprains — most commonly the ACL — cause sudden pain, swelling and instability. Mild and moderate injuries recover fully with structured physiotherapy.
symptoms_html:
• Pain, often sudden and severe
  • A loud pop or snap at the moment of injury
  • Rapid swelling after the injury
  • A feeling of looseness or instability in the joint
  • Inability to put weight on the leg without pain
causes_html:
• ACL injury — the most commonly injured ligament; sudden direction changes, jumping and landing (skiing, basketball, football)
  • PCL injury — direct blow to the knee, often in car accidents; about 20% of ligament injuries
  • MCL injury — pressure on the outside of the knee, common in football
  • LCL injury — force pushing the knee joint from the inside
treatment_html:
The knee has four main ligaments — ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL — and any can be sprained or torn. In mild and moderate injuries, physiotherapy will help you recover fully: reducing swelling, restoring range of motion, then rebuilding strength and stability with progressive exercise.

After surgery

In severe cases where the ligament is completely torn, reconstructive surgery may be required — your orthopaedic surgeon decides based on severity. Post-surgery, physiotherapy is essential: we speed your recovery, restore full knee function and get you back to sport and daily life safely.

name: Hijama Cupping Therapy
summary: Hijama (wet) cupping is a safe, effective procedure with zero side effects that gives immediate relief. Also known as medicinal cupping, it removes toxins and triggers the body's natural healing response.
symptoms_html:
• Chronic back, neck, knee or arthritic pain
  • Tension headaches and migraine
  • Seasonal allergies and sinus trouble
  • Bloating, indigestion and constipation
  • Fatigue, sluggishness and poor circulation
causes_html: Cupping is used when sluggish circulation, toxin build-up and muscle tension keep the body from healing itself. It complements — not replaces — physiotherapy for the conditions above.
treatment_html:
Hijama cupping therapy is very safe and gives immediate relief. Cups create suction on the skin (dry cupping) for 2–3 minutes; for wet cupping, tiny sterile incisions then allow elimination of toxic blood and fluids. Proper sterilisation technique is followed throughout.

Types of cupping

  • Hijama / wet cupping
  • Dry cupping
  • Fire cupping
  • Moving / dynamic cupping

Benefits

  • Pain relief — back, neck, knee, arthritic pain, headache and migraine
  • Sinus discomfort — many patients report easier, freer comfort
  • Skin health — increased blood flow keeps skin glowing and toned
  • Hair growth — scalp cupping removes toxins and stimulates follicles
  • Digestion — helps bloating, ulcers and constipation
  • Relaxation — increased circulation relieves deep tension

When cupping is not used

  • Fractures, bleeding disorders, haemophilia
  • Severe infection or non-compliant patients

name: Physiotherapy for Cerebral Palsy
summary: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of neurological disorders appearing in infancy or early childhood that disrupt the brain's ability to control movement, posture and balance. Physiotherapy maintains and improves a child's abilities at every stage.
symptoms_html:
• Delayed milestones — difficulty sitting, standing or walking
  • Stiff, tight muscles (spasticity) and awkward movements
  • Poor coordination, balance and depth perception
  • Slow, writhing or jerky involuntary movements
  • Increased reflexes and scissor-like leg movement
causes_html:
• Abnormal brain development during pregnancy, birth or early infancy
  • Birth complications and oxygen deprivation
  • Neonatal infections such as meningitis
  • Genetic factors — in many cases the cause is not clear
  • CP is non-progressive: it does not worsen over time
treatment_html:
Cerebral refers to the brain; palsy to loss or impairment of motor function. The four main types are spastic (most common — stiffness and awkward movement), dyskinetic (involuntary writhing movements), ataxic (balance and coordination difficulty) and mixed. Physiotherapy is the most important treatment after diagnosis, focusing on function, movement and the child's abilities.

Our physiotherapy programme

  • Passive stretching — relieves soft-tissue tightness in spastic muscles
  • Joint rotation — neck, shoulder, hip, ankle: reduces stiffness, improves circulation
  • Targeted stretching — calf, quadriceps and hamstrings for toe-walking and stiff knees
  • Strengthening — bridging, cobra position, resistance-band work, dynamic quadriceps, supported squats
  • Core stability — swiss-ball exercises for trunk control
  • Balance & coordination — normal, tandem and sideways walking

A child can attend school while continuing therapy sessions — programmes are built around daily life.

name: Physiotherapy for Scoliosis
summary: Scoliosis is a sideways curvature of the spine affecting any age — most commonly seen in children during growth spurts. Most cases are mild; physiotherapy strengthens the muscles that support the spine and manages the curve.
symptoms_html:
• Uneven shoulders — one higher than the other
  • One hip higher or more prominent
  • One side of the rib cage protruding forward
  • Body leaning to one side
  • A visibly curved spine when bending forward
causes_html:
• Idiopathic — most cases; cause unknown, cannot be prevented
  • Neuromuscular conditions — cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, spinal muscular atrophy, spina bifida
  • Birth defects — abnormal spinal development in the womb
  • Injury or infection of the spine, and spinal cord abnormalities
treatment_html:
Treatment depends on age, curve severity and likelihood of progression. Mild curves need observation only; bracing is used for growing children with curves of 25–40 degrees, worn 15–23 hours a day (successfully stops progression in 80% of children). Surgery is reserved for curves greater than 40 degrees.

How physiotherapy helps

Scoliosis can be managed effectively with physiotherapy. Our physiotherapists focus on strengthening the muscles that support your spine, correcting posture, and prescribing specific exercises depending on whether your case is mild, moderate or severe — reducing pain and limiting curve progression.

name: Physiotherapy for Bell's Palsy
summary: Bell's palsy causes sudden paralysis or weakness on one side of the face — the most common cause of facial paralysis. Early physiotherapy with electrical stimulation and facial exercises significantly improves recovery.
symptoms_html:
• Sudden weakness or paralysis on one side of the face
  • Drooping eyebrow and mouth corner
  • Difficulty closing one eyelid, causing eye dryness
  • Excessive tears in one eye
  • Drooling from one side of the mouth
  • Pain around the jaw and behind the ear
  • Facial pain or abnormal sensations
causes_html:
• Inflammation and swelling of cranial nerve VII (the facial nerve)
  • Dormant viral infections — herpes simplex, varicella (chickenpox)
  • Impaired immunity — stress, sleep deprivation, minor illness, autoimmune syndromes
  • Lyme disease and other facial-nerve inflammations
  • Myelin sheath damage — the fatty insulation around nerve fibres
treatment_html:
Bell's palsy results from a problem in cranial nerve VII, which connects the brain to the muscles of facial expression. Most patients recover — and physiotherapy meaningfully improves the speed and completeness of that recovery.

Physiotherapy treatment

  • Electric stimulation — 30 contractions to maintain muscle tone
  • Galvanic stimulation — for the muscles of the face
  • Faradic stimulation — for the nerve trunk
  • Facial exercises — practiced regularly to retrain expression

Advice for recovery

  • Apply moist heat to paralysed areas to reduce pain; massage gently
  • Keep the face warm — exposure to cold can aggravate paralysis
  • Keep the eye moist: close it manually with a finger, tape it for sleeping, use protective glasses in the shower
  • Eat a balanced diet rich in leafy greens; Vitamin B12, B6 and zinc support nerve growth
  • Manage stress with relaxation exercises; cut food small and chew on the comfortable side
